prompts:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a professional desktop PC game UI CONCEPT presentation for PARVOZ drone simulator, mouse and keyboard. Reference 1 supplies the actual game underground parking environment and selected drone; preserve that recognizable ordinary game environment, do not upgrade it into a fantasy photoreal hangar. Reference 2 shows the old overwordy login for context ONLY; replace its interface completely. These are design mockups, not screenshots of implemented software.
One high resolution portrait board containing TWO large landscape 16:9 game screens stacked vertically, with a thin plain label strip between them. Each screen large and legible, crisp realistic UI typography. Top screen shows authentication with Sign in and Register tabs, bottom screen shows main game menu on left and nonmodal Downloads panel on right. Keep identical information in both variants. English interface to match current game. Only exact text specified, no explanatory prose, no marketing, no gratuitous slogans, no extra invented features. Preserve PARVOZ wordmark. Actual UI labels must use sentence case, no monospaced labels, no letterspacing on tiny text.
AUTH: simple two tabs "Sign in" (active) and "Register"; field labels "Username" and "Password", input value "Pilot" and masked password; one dominant "Sign in" button; subtle text links "Forgot password?" and "Play as guest". No email, social login, remember me, confirm password, new account requirements, or other invented functionality. Registration tab will reuse the same two fields and primary button "Create account", no need to depict that state.
DOWNLOADS: title "Downloads", close X; three compact horizontal rows with small location thumbnail, map name, one status and relevant action. "Minus Two" with "65%" and "67 / 103 MB", progress bar, "Cancel". "Hangar C03" with "Queued" and "Cancel". "Arena" with checkmark "Downloaded". One quiet footer "422 MB on this device". Do not show speed, ETA, pause or delete actions. Underlying main menu remains visible and usable, showing "Fly", "Multiplayer", "Hangar", "Settings"; no explanatory copy anywhere. Font sizes appropriate at 1280x720 game resolution, legible labels, consistent hierarchy, keyboard-focus treatment plausible. Avoid huge headings, rounded SaaS card grids, gradients, futuristic HUD decorations, neon glow, sci-fi bevels, dense marketing labels, fake telemetry, overdesigned icons. Only game-relevant interface.
VARIANT A: restrained PC racing game design, label strip "A · Centered form / compact downloads". Neutral dark gray #23262b surfaces with a subtle warm orange #eea462 accent tied to existing PARVOZ brand, ivory #f0f1f1 text, muted #adb1b7 secondary. Humanist sans-serif like Source Sans 3, medium weight, normal width, clean familiar readability. 4px corner radii, matte opaque panel surfaces, understated separators, no stacked outer decorative border. Authentication is a moderately sized compact CENTERED rectangular dialog over the dimmed game background, around 390px wide at1280px. Tabs on top, fields vertically stacked, primary button full width, forgot password adjacent to password label, guest link below. Form should have comfortable but not excessive space. Downloads is a compact right-side floating panel anchored near the lower-right download launcher, around420px wide, only as tall as its3rows, not stretched full height. Main left navigation remains clean simple text rows with a restrained orange selected row. Keep the drone visible in middle. Draw both screens faithfully as a coherent production-feasible design. Label screens "Sign in" and "Downloads" outside the game frames only.
